source.title: Derry Journal, 6 May 1936, p. 4 ("Dramatic Derry election surprise: Mr. P. Maxwell nominated for North Ward")
source.publisher: Derry Journal (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed (Derry Journal, 6 May 1936: retiring members returned unopposed in the four other wards)

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934: retirement of two councillors and one alderman in each of the five wards of Londonderry Corporation; nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. The fifteen retiring members were expected to be returned unopposed, but Patrick Maxwell, a Nationalist South Ward councillor, was nominated at the last minute for the North Ward councillorships as a protest against the proposed revision of the wards; all other seats were filled unopposed (Derry Journal, 6 and 18 May 1936; News-Letter, 6 and 16 May 1936). Goligher replaced Councillor A. Strange, who did not seek re-election. Returned unopposed.
